body.statement: If a map between normed function spaces is Hadamard differentiable at the population element tangentially to the support of a tight weak limit, then weak convergence of the centered input process implies weak convergence of the centered image process to the derivative applied to that limit.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.9.4 (Delta-method). Let D and E be metrizable topological vector spaces. Let phi:D_phi subset D -> E be Hadamard-differentiable at theta tangentially to D_0. Let X_n:Omega_n -> D_n be maps with r_n(X_n - theta) converging weakly to X for some sequence of constants r_n -> infinity, where X is separable and takes its values in D_0. Then r_n(phi(X_n) - phi(theta)) converges weakly to phi_prime_theta(X). If phi is defined and continuous on the whole of D, then the sequence r_n(phi(X_n) - phi(theta)) - phi_prime_theta(r_n(X_n - theta)) converges to zero in outer probability.
